10.1002_adfm.76813: Against the backdrop of global “dual‐carbon” goals and the rapid expansion of the new energy industry, water electrolysis for hydrogen production has emerged as a pivotal route for transforming the global energy structure. However, its industrial‐scale deployment is hindered by sluggish electrocatalytic reaction kinetics, highlighting the urgent need for high‐performance electrocatalysts to reduce energy barriers. Built‐in electric field (BIEF) engineering has attracted increasing attention because it can accelerate charge transport, regulate the adsorption/desorption behavior of reaction intermediates, enhance intrinsic catalytic activity, and tailor the local reaction microenvironment. Unlike existing reviews that mainly focused on general heterostructure design or charge‐transfer regulation in electrocatalysis, this review provides a systematic overview of BIEF engineering for water electrolysis electrocatalysts. Specifically, the fundamental concepts, formation mechanisms, and intrinsic advantages of BIEFs are summarized, followed by representative modulation strategies, including alloying, heteroatom doping, defect engineering, and heterojunction engineering. Moreover, practical applications of BIEF engineering in n–n, p–n, p–p, and Mott–Schottky heterojunction electrocatalysts are highlighted, establishing the relationship between BIEF construction, interfacial electronic regulation, and electrocatalytic performance enhancement. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are discussed to guide the rational design of advanced BIEF‐driven electrocatalysts.
10.1002_aenm.71725: Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g −1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mg Ir cm −2 , it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm −2 . Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.
10.1002_smll.202510652: Wide bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) play an essential role in tandem solar cell architectures. These architectures represent a promising approach for surpassing the efficiency limits associated with single-junction solar cells. Nevertheless, WBG subcells encounter substantial challenges, particularly those related to inhomogeneous crystallization processes and pronounced non-radiative recombination losses. Additionally, the oxidation of iodide ions during device operation can induce halide segregation, which significantly undermines the operational stability of the devices. In the present study, an effective strategy is introduced through the incorporation of phenylhydrazine derivatives into the perovskite solution. This method simultaneously modulates the crystallization behavior and inhibits iodide oxidation in WBG perovskite. The implementation of this strategy yields high-quality perovskite films and leads to a marked enhancement in the photostability of WBG PSCs. Specifically, inverted single-junction WBG PSCs with a bandgap of 1.77 eV obtained a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.75%, accompanied by exceptional operational stability. Furthermore, by integrating the WBG perovskite subcell with mixed Sn-Pb perovskite subcells, two-terminal all-perovskite tandem solar cells were fabricated, which demonstrated an impressive PCE of 28.63%.
10.1002_smll.74918: Polymer‐based nanocomposite coatings capable of reducing abrasion and inhibiting corrosion simultaneously have great potential in marine metallic equipment. However, realizing composite coatings interfacial adaptability to external dynamic load and saltwater erosion still faces significant challenge. Herein, a marine environment self‐adaptive nanocomposite coating was developed, leveraging frictional heat‐driven solid‐liquid phase transition of hierarchical MXene‐polyethylene glycol (PEG)/fluroresin. The coating takes fluorocarbon resin (FR) as the matrix, incorporating MXene nanosheets chemically grafted with polyethylene glycol (PEG) of different molecular weights. Notably, this coating maintains exceptional lubricity across varying external loads (3N ∼ 5N), achieving a low friction coefficient of 0.047 and wear rate of 11.8×10 − 5 mm 3 /N·m. The low‐friction behavior is primarily attributed to the hierarchical self‐adaptive lubrication strategy: MXene deal with low‐load friction, while higher loads generated friction is resolved through the phase transition capability of PEG. Theoretical calculation results also proved that frictional heat drives the directional migration of MXene‐PEG towards the frictional interface, ensuring self‐adaptive interface. Meanwhile, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements confirmed that the coating exhibits outstanding anti‐corrosion performance. This work develops a hierarchical self‐adaptive coating based on MXene interlayer sliding and PEG solid‐liquid phase transition, enabling the coating to provide reliable anti‐corrosion and wear‐resistant for equipment under complex alternating load conditions.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.158152: This study investigates polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-stabilized carbon black (CB) nanofluids for photothermally assisted alkaline water electrolysis using a 0.5 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) electrolyte. The effects of CB concentration and external irradiation, controlled by varying the distance between a halogen lamp and the electrolysis apparatus, were evaluated in terms of hydrogen production, energy consumption, and efficiency. Irradiation increased electrolyte temperature, current, and hydrogen production, with the strongest enhancement at a lamp distance of 10 cm. At the optimum CB concentration of 0.005 wt%, the time required to produce 60 mL of hydrogen decreased by approximately 15%, while specific electrical energy consumption decreased by 7%–8%. Faradaic efficiency remained close to 100%, and photothermal performance was stable during repeated irradiation and storage. These findings demonstrate the potential of CB nanofluids for photothermal enhancement of alkaline electrolysis while highlighting the importance of thermal management and energy utilization.
10.1039_d5ta09719c: Hybrid co-electrolysis integrates CO 2 reduction with biomass oxidation for efficient formic acid production. Surface-engineered SnO 2 nanoflowers enhance charge transfer, selectivity, and sustainable carbon valorization using earth-abundant catalyst.
10.1039_d6ta02012g: Incorporation of a sulfonate-functionalized three-dimensional Cd( ii ) MOF, BITSP, into PEO-Li resulted in a composite polymer electrolyte (CPE), PEO-10% BITSP-LiClO 4 , which enhances conductivity and hence is utilized for supercapacitor fabrication.
